claims.text: Cast HfMoTaTiZr or WVTaTiCr alloys have coarse dendritic microstructures with grain sizes above 100 μm.
The limited ductility of the cast alloys is caused by segregation and coarse intermetallics.
Cryogenic HPT or ECAP can refine the proposed refractory alloy to grain sizes below 50 nm.
Annealing at 800–900 °C for 10–30 minutes after SPD will precipitate a nano-dispersed Laves phase in the BCC matrix.
Laves-phase nucleation can be kinetically suppressed during SPD so that coarse intermetallic growth does not occur at that stage.
The high density of dislocations and grain boundaries produced by SPD will act as Laves-phase nucleation sites during annealing.
A low annealing temperature and short annealing duration will prevent the Laves phase from coarsening into brittle networks.
Rapid quenching after annealing will stabilize the nanocrystalline microstructure.
A BCC matrix and Laves phase can coexist in Cr-containing HfMoTaTiZr.
The processed alloy will contain 1–5 vol% nano-dispersed Laves phase.
Nanocrystalline BCC grains will strengthen the alloy through grain-boundary or Hall–Petch strengthening.
Nano-dispersed Laves particles will provide Orowan strengthening.
Coherent BCC/Laves interfaces will deflect cracks and retain ductility.
The proposed nanocrystalline dual-phase state will increase hardness by more than 50% relative to the cast baseline.
The proposed material will have a yield strength above 1.5 GPa.
The proposed material will retain more than 10% strain to fracture because continuous brittle intermetallic networks are absent.
Cast Cr-containing HfMoTaTiZr can contain a continuous reticulated interdendritic Laves-phase network.
The cast baseline has less than 15% fracture strain and fails by brittle fracture because of its continuous Laves network.
Exceeding the Laves-phase solvus during annealing will cause coarse intermetallic formation.
If SPD strain is insufficient to produce grains below 50 nm, the resulting coarse-grained dual-phase alloy will show limited strength enhancement.

contradictions.description: The baseline attributes limited ductility and brittle fracture to continuous Laves networks, whereas the cited same-system rationale used in the mechanism states that a continuous reticulated Laves structure hinders crack propagation and compensates for plasticity loss.

The proposed constitution is described as a dual-phase solid-solution strategy that avoids brittle intermetallic formation, but the second phase is explicitly a Laves intermetallic; the proposal actually seeks to control its morphology rather than avoid its formation.
